scope: Theorem 12.1 (Oscillatory integral estimate) of the manuscript “Bochner–Riesz multipliers in three dimensions” (preprints/Bochner-Riesz-Multipliers-in-Three-Dimensions-September-24-2026/Bochner-Riesz-Multipliers-in-Three-Dimensions-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 078 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ea18d159eefcdc7f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 104-105. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix bounded input and output regions Kv, Kx ⊂ R2. For the input patch Kv, fix a class of smooth real phases satisfying the phase assumptions of 104 Section 9, with common domain [0, 1] × R2 × Uv, where Uv is an open neighborhood of Kv. All enlarged patches required by the decomposition, expressed in the original v coordinates, are contained in Uv and obey common bounds. The translated systems are considered on the corresponding bounded rescaled patches described in that section, with the resulting uniform bounds. Throughout the phase domain, ∂vΦ(c, x, v) = ζ(v, x − cv). For each phase and each required original input patch V , the matrix ∂pζ is symmetric and satisfies either a0I ≤ ∂pζ(v, p) ≤ a1I (v ∈ V, p ∈ R2 ), or the same inequality with −∂pζ in place of ∂pζ, with common constants a0 > 0 and a1 for the class. On these original patches, every mixed v, p derivative of total order j of this matrix is bounded by Aj+1(j!)3 for a common A ≥ 1. Fix these constants and all the seminorm bounds of a class of smooth amplitudes B supported in [0, 1]×Kx ×Kv. For every ν > 0 there is a constant Cν, depending only on these fixed data and ν, such that, for every λ ≥ 2, every phase and amplitude in the specified classes, and every f ∈ L3(R2) supported in Kv, ∥Eλf∥L3([0,1]×Kx) ≤ Cνλ−1+ν ∥f∥3, Eλf(c, x) = Z eiλΦ(c,x,v) B(c, x, v)f(v) dv. (12.1)
